create.name: Bodhi College
create.bio:
Bodhi College is a non-sectarian Buddhist teaching charity that focuses on the Buddha's earliest teachings, as recorded in the Pali suttas, and on how they can be lived today. Its founders were Akincano Weber, John Peacock, Christina Feldman and Stephen Batchelor. The core faculty has since grown to take in Bernat Font, Martine Batchelor, River Wolton, Antonia Sumbundu, Yuka Nakamura, Jaya Rudgard and Christoph Köck, with visiting teachers alongside. It belongs to no single Buddhist school, and its teachers are encouraged to bring their own views, so students meet more than one reading of the texts.

Study and practice go together. Courses mix meditation with close reading of early discourses on subjects such as mettā, not-self, dependent arising and the history of Buddhism. Formats include silent residential retreats at venues such as ITC Naarden in the Netherlands, live online courses over several weeks, longer programmes for committed practitioners, group mentoring and self-paced e-courses, offered in English and German. Bursaries are available, several retreats meet European criteria for mindfulness teachers' annual practice, and the college also runs online sangha evenings and a series of public conversations.

courses.title: The Thermals of Awakening
courses.description: A two-week residential course at ITC Naarden in the Netherlands with Ajahn Sucitto and Akincano Weber, following the step-by-step way the Buddha set out the path. Teacher dana is offered separately at the end.

courses.title: The Measuring Mind: Unravelling the Dynamics of Selfing
courses.description: A week-long online retreat with Akincano Weber and Ulla König, built around ordinary days so that sessions at either end frame practice at home and at work.
courses.price: Basic Rate: £89 Standard Rate: £99 Supporter Rate: £109

courses.title: Embodied Presence, Wise and Steady Heart
courses.description: A two-week silent retreat at ITC Naarden, near Amsterdam, in calm, insight and loving-kindness practice, with a one-week option.

courses.title: Mettā in the Heart of Daily Life
courses.description: An online week with Bernat Font and River Wolton on kindness and goodwill as a practice woven through everyday life.
courses.price: Basic Rate: £89 Standard Rate: £99 Supporter Rate: £109

courses.title: Buddhist Pasts and Buddhist Presents: History, Tradition and Contemporary Practice
courses.description: Evening online sessions with Akincano Weber and John Peacock on the world the Buddha lived in and how his community grew, as a way into practising the teachings now.
courses.price: Basic rate: £115 Standard rate: £135 Supporter rate: £155

courses.title: Freedom with(out) Identity
courses.description: A six-week online course, with Martine Batchelor among its teachers, on not-self and emptiness in the early texts and what makes up a sense of identity.
courses.price: Basic rate: £139 Standard rate: £159 Supporter rate: £179

courses.title: After Buddhism and Beyond
courses.description: A twelve-week self-study course of recorded lectures, reflections and discussions on secular dharma, developed by Stephen Batchelor and taken at one's own pace.

free_resources.title: Useful Links and Articles
free_resources.description: A reading and listening list picked by the teachers: sutta translation sites, talk archives, reading lists and recommended books on early Buddhism.

free_resources.title: Glossary
free_resources.description: Short explanations of Pali and other Buddhist terms used on the college's courses.
